MACK DAVE T. SICAT President KAISAKA, Inc. Kaisakapwdcityfed0529@gmail.com Dear Mr. Sicat: This refers to your letter dated January 19, 2023, concerning the alleged non-funding allocation of barangays for Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) and Senior Citizens (SCs) organizations. While there may be barangays that have the funds for the PWDs and SCs organizations, this is not the case in all barangays due to budget constraints. Some barangays have meager budgets, which explains the lack of funding for these organizations. This reality was recognized by the national legislators when they passed the lawl mandating the establishment of PDAO in all local government units, save for barangays. Presently, there is no law that specifically mandates barangays to allocate funding for PWDs and SCs organizations. However, insofar as the funding for the PWDs is concerned, Section 17 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 10070, mandates the Department of Social Welfare and Development—as the ex-officio Chair of the National Council on Disability Affairs—to encourage national government agencies to include in their annual budget the provision of funds for programs and services for PWDs in accordance with their mandates and in accordance with the General Appropriation Act, a portion from the five percent (5%) of Gender and Development budget and from the Internal Revenue Allotment—now referred to as "National Tax Allocation" in light of the Mandanas-Garcia ruling of the Supreme Court—for local government units shall be allocated for the implementation of PDAO programs, projects, and activities. Corollarily, Section 18 thereof expressly mandates the governor, city, and municipal mayor to ensure that the necessary funds are allocated for the implementation of the aforesaid IRR for the benefit of PWDs in their respective jurisdictions.
